name: Nungambakkam
tagline: Consulates, tree-lined avenues and the best cafe cluster in town
description: Central Chennai's smartest address, where colonial bungalows and consulates sit alongside boutique offices on Khader Nawaz Khan Road. Specialty coffee shops, bookstores and restaurants line the same few blocks. Remote workers base here because it is genuinely walkable by Chennai standards and close to everything.
bestFor: Nomads who want the shortest commute to cafes, coworking and business districts.
pros: Densest cluster of laptop-friendly cafes and coworking
Central to both the CBD and the airport road
cons: Among the highest rents in Chennai
Heavy traffic on Sterling and Nungambakkam High Roads
Footpaths are frequently blocked by parked vehicles

name: Adyar
tagline: Riverside suburb of quiet lanes, gardens and old money
description: South of the Adyar river, a settled residential district of low apartment blocks, banyan-shaded lanes and the vast Theosophical Society gardens. Families and academics dominate. It has good bakeries, gyms and grocery shops without the chaos of the centre, and beach access is a ten minute drive.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads and families who prioritise quiet, greenery and steady infrastructure.
pros: Calm residential streets with real tree cover
Strong supply of furnished long-term flats
Close to both the beach and the IT corridor
cons: Some low-lying lanes flood in the northeast monsoon
Getting into the centre at rush hour takes 45 minutes

name: Besant Nagar
tagline: Beach neighbourhood built around Elliot's Beach promenade
description: Chennai's most liveable coastal pocket, arranged in numbered avenues behind Elliot's Beach. Mornings are for sea walks and filter coffee, evenings for the beachfront food stalls. A young professional and expat crowd rents here, and a handful of cafes near the beach road work well for a laptop day.
bestFor: Anyone who wants a daily swim or beach run built into their remote work routine.
pros: Walk to the beach in minutes from most streets
Sea breeze makes the heat noticeably easier
Good cafes, bakeries and a young renting crowd
cons: Rents carry a clear beach premium
Salt air corrodes electronics and fittings
Cyclone season brings flooding and power cuts

name: Mylapore
tagline: Temple tanks, silk shops and the oldest streets in Chennai
description: The cultural core of the city, built around the Kapaleeshwarar temple and its tank. Mornings start with flower sellers and filter coffee on the Mada streets, and the December music season fills the concert halls. Housing mixes old family homes with modest apartment blocks at prices below Nungambakkam.
bestFor: Culture-minded slow travellers who want daily life in a genuinely Tamil neighbourhood.
pros: Deep local character, music, food and markets
Cheaper than the neighbouring central districts
Central, with beach and CBD both close
cons: Narrow congested streets and constant horn noise
Temple festivals bring crowds and road closures
Older buildings, so expect patchy maintenance

name: Velachery
tagline: Affordable high-rise sprawl next to the IT corridor
description: A dense modern suburb of apartment towers, malls and tech workers on the southwest edge of the city. Rents run well below the coastal districts, and the MRTS rail line plus the OMR tech corridor put jobs and services close. It is functional rather than pretty, but the value is real.
bestFor: Budget-conscious remote workers who want a new flat and fast internet over charm.
pros: Clearly cheaper rents than central or coastal Chennai
Modern blocks with lifts, power backup and fibre
Rail link plus quick access to the OMR tech corridor
cons: Notorious for monsoon flooding, it sits on a former lake bed
Little character and heavy traffic around the malls
Long trip to the beach or the historic centre
